indexableObject.name: The Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976
Objective
The Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976 was enacted to provide for the incorporation, regulation, and winding up of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) with a view to developing the rural economy. The Act aims to provide credit and banking facilities, particularly to small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, artisans, and small entrepreneurs, thereby promoting agriculture, trade, commerce, industry, and other productive activities in rural areas. 
Key Provisions
•	Establishment of Regional Rural Banks: Provides for the establishment and incorporation of Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) by the Central Government in consultation with the concerned State Government and sponsor bank. 
•	Capital and Shareholding: Prescribes the authorised and issued capital of RRBs and provides for shareholding by the Central Government, State Government, and Sponsor Bank. 
•	Management: Provides for the constitution of a Board of Directors, appointment of the Chairman and staff, and lays down provisions relating to the governance and management of RRBs. 
•	Banking Functions: Authorises RRBs to undertake banking business, including accepting deposits, providing loans and advances, and offering other financial services to rural communities. 
•	Accounts and Audit: Requires RRBs to maintain proper accounts, prepare annual reports, and have their accounts audited in accordance with the Act. 
•	Amalgamation and Winding Up: Provides for the amalgamation, reorganisation, and winding up of Regional Rural Banks under specified circumstances. 
•	Government Control and Rule-making: Empowers the Central Government to issue policy directions and make rules, while RRBs may frame regulations for carrying out the provisions of the Act.

indexableObject.name: The Delivery of Books and Newspapers (Public Libraries) Act, 1954

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Delivery of Books and Newspapers (Public Libraries) Act, 1954

Key Provisions: 
1. Scope: - Extends to the whole of India (initially except Jammu and Kashmir, but now applicable as per notification S.O. 3912(E), dated 30th October, 2019).
•	Applies to the National Library at Calcutta and up to three other libraries specified by the Central Government.

2.	Delivery Requirements: - Books: Publishers must deliver a copy of every newly published book to the National Library and one copy to each of the other specified public libraries within 30 days, free of cost.
•	Copy for the National Library: Complete with all maps and illustrations, on the best paper, and properly bound.
•	Copies for other libraries: On the paper used for the largest print run, in the condition prepared for sale.
•	Exemption: Second or subsequent editions without changes, if a previous edition was already delivered.
•	Newspapers: Publishers must deliver one copy of each issue to specified public libraries as soon as published, free of cost.

3.	Receipt and Penalty: - Receipt: Public libraries must provide a written receipt for delivered books.
•	Penalty for Non-compliance: Fine up to fifty rupees (potentially plus the book's value for book non-delivery), with possible compensation to the affected library.

4.	Jurisdiction and Rules: - Cognizance of Offences: Only courts of presidency magistrates or magistrates of the first class and above, on complaint from an officer empowered by the Central Government.
•	Power to Make Rules: Central Government can make rules to carry out the Act's provisions, with rules laid before Parliament.

5.	Special Provisions: - Government Publications: Act applies to books and newspapers published by the Government, except those for official use only.

2[(3) All acts done by a majority by those present and voting at a meeting of the Trustees, and all acts done in pursuance of a majority decision of the Trustees obtained by circulation to the Trustees of the matter requiring decision, shall be deemed to be acts of the Trustees.]
3[(3A) If any of the Trustees referred to in clauses (b), (d), (e), (f), (g) and (h) of sub-section (1) is unable to attend any meeting of the Trustees, he may, with the previous approval of the Chairman, authorise in writing a person to do so.]
(4) No act of the Trustees shall be, deemed to be invalid merely by reason of any vacancy in, or defect in the constitution of the body of the Trustees.
(5) In the case of ex officio Trustees the person for the time being performing the duties of any of the offices mentioned in sub-section (1) shall act as a Trustee.
(6) The Trustees may appoint a person to act as their Secretary.
(7) Orders for the payment of money on behalf of the Trustees shall be deemed to be sufficiently authenticated if signed by two Trustees and countersigned by the Secretary.
